default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-578.title: Thin-volume micro-break fade
E-578.hypothesis: A poke beyond the recent high/low made on volume below normal for the minute of day has no real participation behind it; liquidity takers are absent and the poke is rejected back into the range.

E-579.title: Tweezer reversal after a run
E-579.hypothesis: Two adjacent bars of opposite colour stopping at the same extreme after a run show a level that two waves of aggressive orders both failed to pass; fade it.

E-580.title: Staircase stall fade
E-580.hypothesis: After a run of bars each making higher highs and higher lows, the first bar that fails to extend and closes down shows the late trend followers have run out of buyers.

E-581.title: Open-chop micro-break fade
E-581.hypothesis: When price has repeatedly crossed the day's opening price in the last 90 minutes the market is rotating around a fair value; short-window breaks in that state are stop runs that revert.

E-582.title: Afternoon micro-break fade
E-582.hypothesis: In the afternoon, after the day's information is priced and before the closing flow, short-window breaks lack follow-through and are faded by liquidity providers.

E-583.title: Close-location saturation fade
E-583.hypothesis: When bars keep closing at one end of their range over a window, aggressors have been paying the spread for a while; that pressure is spent and the next move is back.

E-584.title: Narrow-poke break fade
E-584.hypothesis: A break of the recent extreme made by a small-range bar is a creep rather than an impulse; a creep into resting orders gets absorbed instead of continuing.

E-585.title: One-colour bar share fade
E-585.hypothesis: When nearly all bars in a window have the same colour, the move is one-sided enough that dip buyers or rally sellers are waiting; fade the saturation point.

E-586.title: Local-median stretch fade
E-586.hypothesis: A close far from its rolling median, scaled by the mean absolute deviation around that median, is a robust measure of overextension that single spikes do not distort; fade it.

E-587.title: Early-session micro-break fade
E-587.hypothesis: Right after the open, quotes are wide and breaks of the first few minutes' extremes are often liquidity vacuums, which refill and revert.
